fact: The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunications issued the National Telecommunications Policy (NTP-2004) in January 2004 as the government's policy statement for the telecommunications sector, stating the policy of Government throughout.
The full text of the NTP-2004 is held on the Ministry's official site (mitci.govmu.org), uploaded there in 2025; the document itself is dated January 2004.
The NTP-2004 states no period for the policy, only targets dated 2005 to 2008, and says Government may review and update it at intervals.

The NTP-2004 sets dated targets without costs: fixed density from 28% to 35% and mobile density from 37% to 50% by 2005, broadband to all business hubs by 2006, and 30% of households on broadband and 50% on Internet by 2008; it also commits to a Convergence Act by end December 2004.

The NTP-2004 says the Ministry of IT and Telecommunications is responsible for elaborating the sector policies and gives the regulatory authority (ICTA, set up under the ICT Act 2001) the regulatory tasks it sets out.
The NTP-2004 states no budget for the policy; it proposes a Universal Service Fund raised as a percentage of operator revenue, to be set up by the regulator.

The Ministry of Information Technology and Telecommunications issued the National ICT Policy 2007-11 in September 2007, with a foreword by the Minister calling it the first comprehensive ICT Policy; its cover page also carries the header 2nd Version, 3 August 2007.
The full text of the National ICT Policy 2007-11 is held on the Ministry's official site (mitci.govmu.org), uploaded there in 2025; the document itself is dated September 2007.
The policy is titled 2007-11 and its foreword refers to the coming five years.

The policy says its implementation depends on a National ICT Strategic Plan (NICTSP) setting out the programmes and projects for the next five years; the policy itself gives no costs and the plan is not in this document.
